intended_object: The duality between limits and colimits: a cone t over F is a limit cone if and only if its opposite cocone t.op over F.op is a colimit cocone. This is stated in the docstring and given as an equivalence of the (subsingleton) types of witnesses.
explanation: The body uses IsLimit.op and isLimitOfOp, which convert between a limit cone and a colimit of its opposite cocone. Both IsLimit t and IsColimit t.op are subsingletons, so equivOfSubsingletonOfSubsingleton turns these two maps into an equivalence. That is exactly the type-level form of the docstring's "if and only if". It holds for an arbitrary category C, an arbitrary index category J and any functor and cone, which is the natural generality. The to_dual attribute supplies the dual statement for cocones.
